title: Tuesday, September 15, 2026

headline.title: Monday's leaderboard ran backwards and the day's cleanest move came from the Senate, not the Fed. Energy took the top spot at XLE +2.17% while communications — Monday's best sector at +2.19% — gave back 0.90%, and semiconductors steadied at +0.11% after losing 4.75% the day before. Two sessions, two complete inversions, and neither one caused by a datapoint. The 10-year touched 5.045% intraday, its highest level since 2007, before settling on the 5% line.
headline.summary: The CLARITY Act procedural vote failed in the Senate, and you can see the exact half-hour it happened. COIN and HOOD both printed their session lows in the same 30-minute bar — COIN to 168.07 on 2.8 million shares, HOOD to 105.86 on 3.1 million. From there the two names did opposite things: COIN closed 172.11, near its low, down 7.1%, while HOOD recovered most of the break to close 110.45, down 3.39%. Bitcoin slid into the $76,800 range. That was the only clean single-catalyst move of the session, and it had nothing to do with AI or the Fed.

what_happened: The rotation inverted for the second consecutive session.

Monday: XLC +2.19%, SMH −4.75%. Tuesday: XLE +2.17%, XLC −0.90%, SMH +0.11%. The best sector became a laggard and the worst sector stopped falling, inside 24 hours, with no economic release in between. XLY was the worst at −1.75% and XLU −1.20% registered the yield move. What this says about Monday's AI split is uncomfortable but honest: a rotation that reverses this fast was positioning, not conviction. The essay moved money on Monday and Jensen Huang moved it back on Tuesday, and neither man produced a number.
Oil ran the opposite intraday shape from Monday, which is what made it work.

Monday USO opened at its high of 160.15 and sold all session to close 156.66. Tuesday it opened at 158.38, essentially its low, and climbed all day to a 163.35 high before closing 161.86, +3.32%. Same direction on the headline, opposite structure underneath — and this time the equities followed: XLE +2.17%, the best sector on the board, after closing red on Monday's spike. WTI settled near $104 (+2.6%) and Brent near $108 (+2.1%). Monday the producers disbelieved the barrel; Tuesday they bought it.
CrowdStrike did not give it back, which was not the expectation.

The morning report had CRWD in the 'giving it back' group at −1.91% premarket, with the whole safety complex unwinding. It closed +3.02% at 242.49, near its session high of 243.98 — a third straight advance and into all-time-high territory. The board flags it at 62% bullish options flow with a $2.4M block. The unwind thesis was right about PANW, ZS and FTNT and wrong about the name that led.
Oscar Health spent the day before its Investor Day going down.

OSCR opened 33.57, made its high in the first ten minutes at 33.72, and faded for the rest of the session to close 32.44 — down 4.05% and within seven cents of its low. It surrendered the entire +3.17% gain from Monday the session before presenting long-term financial targets. Going into an event weak is a materially different setup than going in extended, and our five-event study is mostly built on names that gapped up into their events and then failed.

picks.right_note: MORNING CALLS · 3 OF 5 RESOLVED AS WRITTEN
rows: T2 CALL · NAMED THE RIGHT RISK
Morning report: “the thing that can actually move the whole tape is the bond market… the real risk today is not the AI debate at all.”

It touched 5.045% intraday, the highest since 2007, before settling on the 5% line. The rate-sensitive sectors registered it — XLU −1.20%, XLY −1.75% — while the AI complex the headlines were chasing finished roughly flat. Ranking the bond market above the story everyone was watching was the correct read.
Morning report: “fading into its own 12:00 CT keynote — the pattern this book flagged. Faded both prior years.”

Closed −1.46% on keynote day. This is the call that lost on Monday, when CRM closed +4.73% against the same thesis. It was right on the second attempt, which is worth stating plainly rather than claiming the original call was vindicated — a day late is a day late. The real test is Wednesday's Investor & Analyst Session, the half that carries a financial framework.
GAPPED INTO THE PRINT · AS CALLED
Morning report flagged it at −13.46% premarket on a triple miss — revenue $544.1M vs $556.8M, EBITDA $98.9M vs $120.4M, and an unexpected 27c loss against an 18c expected profit.

It closed down 15.6%, worse than the premarket gap. The pattern this book has tracked all month — closing UP into your own print, then missing — produced its cleanest example yet: PLAY closed +4.05% on Monday, the session before the miss.
Morning report ranked it T1: “semis green, safety red — Monday's trade running exactly backwards.”

The first half held and the second half did not. Semis did steady — SMH +0.11% after −4.75% — and PANW, ZS and FTNT did fade. But CRWD, the name that defined the safety bucket, closed +3.02% near its high. Calling the whole bucket red because most of it was red premarket missed that the leader was behaving differently from its followers.
Morning report: “the $13B 20-year auction at 12:00 CT is the live test… watch the tail.”

No auction result in hand at the time of writing, so this is not being scored either way. What is known is that the 10-year touched its highest level since 2007 the same session, which is the environment the auction priced into. Recorded here as an open item rather than a win.

how_played_out: The two-day inversion is the finding, and it undercuts the conviction in both days.

Monday's AI split was real, held every hour, and widened into the close — this book said so and it was correct. Tuesday it reversed almost exactly, and that reversal is evidence about what Monday actually was. A sector rotation driven by an essay on Saturday and a CEO comment on Monday night is positioning moving, not capital being reallocated on a changed view of earnings. The honest conclusion: the AI-slowdown trade has produced two large, opposite moves and zero datapoints. MU on 9/30 is the first real test.
The clean trade of the day was legislative and it was visible in the tape to the half hour.

COIN and HOOD both bottomed in the same 30-minute bar as the CLARITY Act vote failed — COIN at 168.07 on 2.8M shares, HOOD at 105.86 on 3.1M. What happened next separated them: COIN closed near its low at 172.11 while HOOD recovered to 110.45, giving back only a third of its break. Same catalyst, same minute, different structural exposure — HOOD's crypto revenue is a slice of a brokerage, COIN's is the business. The recovery differential was the tradeable information, not the headline.
Ranking the bond market above the loudest story on the tape was the session's best decision.

Every headline Tuesday was AI or Fed. The morning report put the 10-year at 5% in the T2 slot and said explicitly that the AI debate was not the day's real risk. The 10-year then printed 5.045%, its highest since 2007. It did not break the equity tape — that is the part still pending — but it moved to a level that makes Wednesday's dot plot considerably more dangerous than the 93%-priced decision attached to it.

The candle says nothing: opened 213.33, ranged 211.16–213.94, closed 212.17, +0.57%. The flow says everything — a $1.2B bid-side print after hours, third straight night as the board's largest single name, and the opposite side of Monday's $796M ask.

Size working both sides of one name into a decision is a hedge being built, not a directional signal.

darkpool.note: Roughly $5B of S&P 500 tracker size printed after hours, all of it bid-side, the night before a near-certain rate hike. VOO $1.8B (bid) topped the whole board — the seventh straight session an S&P tracker has been the tape's largest print — with IVV $1.7B (bid) and SPY $1.5B (bid) behind it. Index money repositioning into an event, and the lean-not-verdict caveat applies twice over on index flow. The mega-caps leaned the same way: NVDA, AMD, MSFT, AVGO and AAPL all printed at the bid. MU and PLTR took the ask instead — and MU has taken over the top of cumulative flow at $4.9B (mixed), ahead of NVDA $4.3B (bid) and META $3.1B (ask).
darkpool.right_note: The board is working both ends of the clock. Largest block: ICE $145C 09/18 at $26.8M, a floor call block expiring Friday on triple witching, two days after the decision. Largest sweep: META $670C 01/21/28 at $4.6M, dated to January 2028, on the name carrying $3.1B of ask-side cumulative flow. One ticket pointed at Friday, one at 2028.

watchlist.em_label: CLOSES VS MONDAY 9/14 — EVERY MONDAY LEADER GAVE IT BACK

lessons: A rotation that reverses inside 24 hours was positioning, not conviction.

Monday's split was real and this book called it correctly. Tuesday it inverted almost exactly — XLE took the lead, XLC gave back, SMH steadied — and that reversal is evidence about what Monday was. Capital does not reallocate on a changed earnings view and then change back overnight. Two large opposite moves, zero datapoints, both sourced to executives talking. Treat the next leg the same way until a number arrives, and the first number is MU on 9/30.
When one name in a bucket behaves differently from the bucket, the name is the signal.

The morning call put CRWD in the 'giving it back' group because PANW, ZS, FTNT and NET were all red premarket. Those four faded and CRWD closed +3.02% near its high. The leader of a rotation and its followers are not the same trade, and grouping them cost the call. When the name that created a move is diverging from the names that joined it, that divergence deserves its own line rather than an average.
A legislative catalyst prints at a specific minute, and the recovery is the tradeable part.

COIN and HOOD bottomed in the same 30-minute bar on the CLARITY Act failure — and then did completely different things, COIN closing near its low and HOOD recovering two thirds of the break. The headline was identical for both; the structural exposure was not. On event-driven breaks, the first thirty minutes tells you what happened and the next two hours tell you who actually had to sell.
Ranking the quiet risk above the loud story was correct, and it is still pending.

Every headline was AI or Fed; the report put the 10-year in the T2 slot and said the AI debate was not the real risk. It printed 5.045%, the highest since 2007. It has not broken the equity tape yet — which is precisely why it stays the thing to watch into a dot plot rather than being marked as a finished call.
tomorrow: The decision is 93% priced. The dot plot is not. A 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% at 1:00 CT is confirmation, not information. June's plot penciled one more 2026 hike; futures lean two by year-end — that gap is the actual event, and Warsh's minimalist communication style makes the dots louder than the presser.

August retail sales at 7:30 CT, seen +0.9% after July's −0.6%, the biggest monthly drop in over a year. BofA card data still shows spending up 4.5% year-over-year, so this is genuinely open. It lands five and a half hours before the decision, so the tape reprices twice.

OSCR's Investor Day is 8:00 CT and it goes in weak, having closed −4.05%. Our five-event study says watch volume in the first thirty minutes — the ratio ordered the range almost perfectly across all five. The 2024 event ran an 11.90% intraday range; the money was in the path, not the close.
CRM's Investor & Analyst Session is 3:00 CT, at the bell on decision day — the half of Dreamforce that carries a financial framework. The keynote faded as called; this is the real test.
LEN reports after the close, Street near $1.30 and expected lower year-over-year — a homebuilder printing hours after a rate hike with mortgage rates north of 7%.
